newsitem.title: UK: Lucas adopts shift to EVA with Varity merger.
newsitem.headline: Lucas adopts shift to EVA with Varity merger.

text.p: The five businesses forming Lucas Industries, now merged into LucasVarity Plc, posted "quite significant" gains in EVA (economic value added) in the last financial year, finance director John Grant said on Tuesday.
Commenting on Lucas' last solo results, for the year to July 31, Grant said all its automotive and aerospace components units were at least EVA neutral, "and most are EVA positive".

Victor Rice, who came from the former Varity Corp to be managing director of the merged group, has laid down EVA -- defined as operating income less the cost of capital -- as "a cultural imperative" at LucasVarity and a fundamental monitor.

Grant told Reuters in a telephone interview that Lucas managers had responded to the EVA approach, which Rice has said needs to be used as a guide for every business unit, product development programme, capital projuect and business plan.

"We're already noticing some changes in behaviour -- EVA is proving an easier mechanism for people to balance the priorities between cash and profit, which we used to look at separately," he explained.
Because the use of residual profit equations like EVA also targets the creation of sustainable cash flow to feed back to shareholders, managers like Rice see it as a share price driver.

Rice told a May briefing to financial analysts at the time of the merger announcement that, "there is a direct correlation between EVA and share price. If it does not produce an after-tax return comfortably above our cost of capital, it doesn't increase EVA, and it won't fly at LucasVarity".
Grant said that, logically, EVA had to be forward looking and be about creating future growth as well as earnings.

"Its open-ended nature is encouraging people to think more vigorously about profitability, both through returns on capital and through growth -- you really have to grow the business as well," he added. The finance director noted that detailed EVA numbers were not being announced with the final Lucas Industries numbers.
The first combined LucasVarity accounts will be for the period to January 31, 1997 -- in line with Varity's traditional full year -- and are due in April. EVA should figure highly.
